speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient presents with a 3-day history of pain in his left wrist, which worsened this morning accompanied by chills and malaise. He recounts having a self-resolving left knee pain the previous week. Reports recent return from a camping trip in Minnesota. Sexually active with one female partner. No history of trauma to the wrist.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Lyme Disease (Erythema Migrans with arthritis)

The history of camping in Minnesota, recent knee pain, and now a warm, swollen wrist strongly suggests Lyme disease from a tick bite. Given your age and travel history, I suspect the "skin lesions" might be the expanding rash of Erythema Migrans or related erythema. Do you recall any specific rash appearing on your body recently, and can you show me photos of it? I will also request an images review of your wrist and any skin findings.

REQUEST TEST: Lyme_Serology (ELISA/Western Blot)
